expectations.description: Warns against adding modifications purely to improve fit (MI-chasing)
expectations.evidence: Directly warns against 'MI-chasing' and describes it as 'mining your data for post-hoc adjustments'

expectations.description: Uses or invokes the concept of 'capitalization on chance' or 'overfit' or 'sample-specific'
expectations.evidence: Uses the phrase 'capitalizing on chance' and references 'idiosyncratic features of your particular sample'

expectations.description: Recommends substantive justification for any modification
expectations.evidence: Explicitly asks for 'a plausible substantive reason this parameter should exist, independent of the fact that it improves fit' and gives examples (shared item wording, method effects)

expectations.description: Recommends cross-validation, replication, or holdout sample if modifications are made
expectations.evidence: States 'the resulting model should be validated in an independent sample or via cross-validation before it's presented as a confirmed structure'

expectations.description: States that the resulting model should be characterized as exploratory/respecified, not confirmatory
expectations.evidence: States 'A model that started as CFA but incorporated data-driven modifications is no longer a confirmatory model — it's an exploratory respecification'

expectations.description: Suggests examining standardized residuals to understand WHERE the model misfits
expectations.evidence: Recommends 'Examine the matrix of standardized residual covariances' to understand 'which specific item pairs are being poorly reproduced'

expectations.description: Does not endorse adding the MIs without any caveats
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'No — you shouldn't just add those modifications and report the improved model without careful caveats' and maintains this throughout
